name: LM4132AMF-3.3_NOPB
title: SOT-23 precision low-dropout series voltage reference, 20 mA, with enable
summary: The LM4132 is a CMOS band-gap series voltage reference in SOT-23-5, trimmed after packaging through on-chip EEPROM. It comes in six fixed voltages from 1.8 V to 4.096 V and five accuracy grades, the A grade at 0.05% and 10 ppm/°C. It sources 20 mA, draws 60 µA, drops out at 400 mV, needs no output capacitor but accepts up to 10 µF, and shuts down to 3 µA from its enable pin. The LM4132-Q1 is the automotive version. LM4132AMF-3.3/NOPB is the 3.3 V A-grade part on a 1000-piece reel.
key_figures: 10 ppm/°C max (0 to 85°C), 20 ppm/°C max (-40 to 125°C)
175 mV typ at 10 mA, 400 mV max

notes: Grades A to E set initial accuracy and temperature coefficient: A 0.05% and 10 ppm/°C (0 to 85°C), B 0.1%, C 0.2%, D 0.4%, E 0.5% and 30 ppm/°C.
MF parts come on a 1000-piece reel and MFX on 3000; the Q1 automotive parts come as MFR (3000) or MFT (250).
A suffix .A or .B after the number is a separate orderable code for the same device.

pins.name: EN
pins.function: Enable. Above 65% of VIN the reference runs, below 35% of VIN it shuts down; an internal pull-up of about 2 µA lets it float. Must not exceed VIN.

pins.function: Supply input; needs a ceramic capacitor to ground.

pins.name: VREF
pins.function: Reference output, up to 20 mA (25 mA for LM4132-3.3-Q1).

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The reference on its own: a 5 V supply into VIN with its input capacitor, the enable line brought out, and a 2.5 V output with an optional output capacitor. The input capacitor must be at least as large as the output capacitor, and 0.1 µF or more when there is none.

parts.note: ceramic X5R or X7R, required, CIN ≥ COUT

circuits.title: Voltage reference with complementary output
circuits.description: An op amp on ±5 V inverts the reference with two equal resistors, giving -VREF beside +VREF. The non-inverting input returns to ground through R/2. The output capacitor sits between 4.7 µF and 10 µF.

circuits.title: Precision voltage reference with force and sense output
circuits.description: A buffer amplifier on a single 5 V supply drives the load from VREF_FORCE and takes its feedback from VREF_SENSE, so the reference reaches the far end of the load wiring. The reference output carries 0.1 µF and a 100 kΩ load to ground.

circuits.title: Programmable current source
circuits.description: The reference's ground pin floats on top of the load. VREF across R1 plus the rheostat RSET sets a current that, with the part's own ground current, flows down through the 1 kΩ load RL: IOUT = VREF / (R1 + RSET) + IGND. A 0.1 µF capacitor sits from VREF to the floating ground pin.

parts.note: variable; wiper joined to the end at R1

operation.text: A CMOS band-gap series reference whose curvature, temperature coefficient and initial accuracy are trimmed through EEPROM registers after packaging, so assembly shift is corrected. It sources up to 20 mA and needs no output capacitor or buffer.

Fixed outputs of 1.8, 2.048, 2.5, 3.0, 3.3 and 4.096 V, with custom voltages from 1.8 V to 4.096 V offered. Five grades: A at 0.05% initial accuracy and 10 ppm/°C (0 to 85°C, 20 ppm/°C over -40 to 125°C), down to E at 0.5% and 30 ppm/°C. The LM4132-Q1 is AEC-Q100 qualified, temperature grade 1 (-40 to 125°C ambient), HBM ESD class 2.
Runs from VREF + 400 mV up to 5.5 V at 10 mA load, drawing 60 µA typical. A ceramic input capacitor close to the part is required.

EN above 65% of VIN turns the reference on; between 0 V and 35% of VIN turns it off, and supply current falls to 3 µA typical. EN can be tied to VIN so the output comes up with the supply. An internal pull-up of roughly 2 µA lets EN float. EN above VIN stops correct operation.
The output survives a short to ground indefinitely, the current being held to 75 mA.
Time for the output to reach 90% of its final value grows with load capacitance: typically 33.2 µs into 1 µF and 78.8 µs into 10 µF. At -40°C during brownout it can stretch to as long as 10 ms.

CIN is a small X5R or X7R ceramic, never smaller than COUT, and at least 0.1 µF when there is no output capacitor. A larger CIN of about 4.7 µF to 22 µF lowers output noise and start-up overshoot; an added bypass from input to ground can lower noise further. With CIN fitted the part drives any load up to VREF / 20 mA of resistance and 10 µF of capacitance. The output is stable with no capacitor or up to 10 µF; a capacitor helps a light-to-heavy load step, but a large one slows turn-on and line and load transients. Low-ESR ceramics are the usual choice, mounted close to the pins.
Typically 50 ppm over 1000 hours, measured on 5 units of each voltage at 5 V input, no load, room temperature.

Board stress shifts the output. Stress is greatest near the middle of a board, so the part is better placed near an edge or corner. A U-shaped slot cut round three sides of the part isolates it mechanically and also thermally. SOT-23 references are less sensitive to assembly stress than SOIC parts. CIN goes close to VIN and GND, COUT close to VREF and GND.
ESD protection is limited; keep leads shorted or the part in conductive foam in storage and handling.
